title.rendered: Heat Pump Vs Air Conditioning Unit: Which is Best in Burnaby?

content.rendered:
If you’ve been sweating through Burnaby’s increasingly warm summers while also dreading the damp chill of our coastal winters, you’ve probably found yourself comparing a heat pump vs air conditioning unit and wondering which one actually makes sense for your home. It’s one of the most common questions homeowners in the Lower Mainland ask us, and honestly, there isn’t a one-size-fits-all answer. It depends on your home, your budget, and how you actually use your space throughout the year.

Let’s break it down so you can make a decision that fits your household, not just a sales pitch.

What is a Heat Pump and How Does it Work

Before comparing the two, it helps to understand what a heat pump is and how it works. Unlike a furnace that burns fuel to create heat, a heat pump moves heat from one place to another. In the winter, it extracts warmth from the outside air (yes, even cold air holds thermal energy) and pumps it inside your home. In the summer, it simply reverses the cycle, pulling heat out of your house and releasing it outdoors functioning exactly like an air conditioner.

This dual functionality is the biggest draw of heat pump air conditioning systems. You get heating and cooling from a single unit, which is a huge advantage in a climate like Burnaby’s, where winters are mild enough that a heat pump can handle most of your heating needs without backup, while summers are warm enough to justify proper cooling.

Air Conditioning Units: The Traditional Cooling Choice

A standalone air conditioning unit, on the other hand, does one job: it cools. It works by cycling refrigerant through indoor and outdoor coils, absorbing heat from inside your home and releasing it outside. It’s a tried-and-tested technology, and for homes that already have a reliable furnace for winter heating, adding a dedicated AC unit for summer comfort can be a straightforward, cost-effective solution.

The catch is that you’re running two separate systems: a furnace for winter and an AC unit for summer which means two systems to maintain, repair, and eventually replace.

Comparing Costs: Heat Pump vs Air Conditioning Unit

Cost is usually the deciding factor for most Burnaby homeowners, so let’s talk numbers.

The cost of air conditioning installation on its own tends to be lower upfront than installing a full heat pump system, simply because you’re only paying for a cooling appliance. If your furnace is still in good shape and you just want relief from summer heat, a standalone AC unit might seem like the cheaper route initially.

However, when you factor in the cost of fitting air conditioning alongside the ongoing expense of running a separate gas or electric furnace, the math starts to shift. Heat pumps are more energy-efficient than furnaces for most of the year in our mild coastal climate, which often means lower utility bills over time. Many Burnaby homeowners also qualify for rebates through BC Hydro and FortisBC when switching to a heat pump, which can significantly offset the initial investment.

So while a heat pump typically has a higher upfront air conditioning unit installation cost compared to a basic AC system, it can pay for itself over a few years through energy savings and rebate programs plus you’re getting heating and cooling in one package instead of two separate systems.

Which One Suits Burnaby’s Climate Better?

Burnaby sits in a temperate coastal zone. Our winters rarely dip to extreme lows for extended periods, and our summers, while getting hotter each year with more frequent heat waves, aren’t as brutal as inland or prairie climates. This kind of moderate climate is actually ideal for heat pumps.

Because heat pumps don’t have to fight against extreme cold, they can operate efficiently through most of a Burnaby winter, only needing backup heating during the rare deep freeze. And when summer rolls around, that same unit switches over and cools your home just as effectively as a standard air conditioner.

If you live in an older Burnaby home with an aging furnace, replacing it with a heat pump system often makes more financial and practical sense than installing a separate AC unit and keeping an outdated furnace running for another decade.

Don’t Forget Maintenance

Whichever system you choose, regular upkeep matters. Air conditioning maintenance things like cleaning coils, replacing filters, checking refrigerant levels, and inspecting ductwork keeps your system running efficiently and extends its lifespan. The same applies to heat pumps, which technically need a bit more attention since they run year-round rather than just in summer.

Skipping maintenance is one of the fastest ways to see your energy bills creep up and your system fail earlier than it should. A quick seasonal check-up from a licensed technician can catch small issues before they become expensive repairs.

So, Which Should You Choose?

Here’s the honest, no-fluff answer:

  • Choose a heat pump if your furnace is aging, you want to reduce your carbon footprint, you’re eligible for rebates, or you want one system that handles both heating and cooling efficiently in Burnaby’s mild climate.
  • Choose a standalone air conditioning unit if your furnace is relatively new and reliable, your budget is tighter right now, and you mainly need summer cooling without touching your heating setup.

Both options work well in Burnaby; it really comes down to your home’s current setup, how long you plan to stay in it, and how much you value long-term efficiency versus lower upfront costs.

Get Expert Advice for Your Burnaby Home

Every home is different, and the best way to decide between a heat pump and an air conditioning unit is to have a professional assess your space, your existing HVAC setup, and your budget. Our team at Airlinx Heating has helped countless Burnaby homeowners navigate this exact decision, and we’re happy to walk you through your options, provide accurate cost estimates, and recommend the system that actually fits your home rather than pushing a one-size-fits-all solution.

Reach out today for a free consultation, and let’s figure out the best heating and cooling solution for your Burnaby home.

title.rendered: What Is HVAC? A Complete Guide to Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning

content.rendered:
If you’ve ever wondered what is HVAC while reading a home listing, getting a repair quote, or noticing your energy bill creep up, you’re not alone. HVAC is one of those terms everyone hears but few people fully understand  until something breaks down on the coldest night of the year. This guide breaks down what does HVAC stand for, how the system works, and why choosing the right HVAC contractor matters just as much as the equipment itself.

Whether you’re a homeowner in Burnaby researching HVAC Services Burnaby or a business owner planning an upgrade, this guide will give you a clear, practical understanding of your heating and cooling system.

What Does HVAC Stand For?

Let’s start with the basics. HVAC meaning: HVAC stands for Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning. It’s the umbrella term for the systems and equipment responsible for regulating indoor temperature, humidity, and air quality in homes, offices, and commercial buildings.

So, what is Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning, exactly? It’s the combination of three connected functions:

  • Heating – Warms indoor spaces during cold months using furnaces, boilers, or heat pumps.
  • Ventilation – Circulates and exchanges air to remove pollutants, odors, and excess moisture while bringing in fresh outdoor air.
  • Air Conditioning – Cools and dehumidifies indoor air during warmer months for comfort and air quality control.

Together, these three components work as a single integrated system to keep your indoor environment comfortable, healthy, and energy-efficient year-round.

How Does an HVAC System Work?

An HVAC system doesn’t just “make it warm” or “make it cool”  it’s a coordinated network of components working together:

  1. Thermostat – Sets the desired temperature and signals the system to turn on or off.
  2. Furnace or Heat Pump – Generates or transfers heat throughout the building.
  3. Air Conditioner or Heat Pump (Cooling Mode) – Removes heat and humidity from indoor air.
  4. Ductwork – Distributes conditioned air throughout the space.
  5. Ventilation System – Exchanges stale indoor air for fresh outdoor air.
  6. Air Filters – Trap dust, allergens, and particles to improve indoor air quality.

When one part of this chain isn’t working properly, comfort and efficiency suffer  which is why professional HVAC installation and regular upkeep are so important.

Why HVAC Systems Matter for Your Home or Business

A well-functioning HVAC system does more than control temperature. It affects:

  • Indoor air quality – Filtering allergens, dust, and pollutants
  • Energy efficiency – Reducing utility costs through optimized performance
  • Comfort – Maintaining consistent temperature and humidity year-round
  • Property value – Modern, efficient systems are a selling point for homes and commercial buildings
  • Health and safety – Preventing mold growth, poor air circulation, and carbon monoxide risks

This is why investing in the right HVAC solutions, not just any equipment, but a system matched to your building’s size and needs  makes a measurable difference over time.

Types of HVAC Services You Should Know About

Understanding HVAC services helps you know what to expect and when to call a professional.

1. HVAC Installation

New construction, renovations, or replacing an outdated system all require professional HVAC installation. Correct sizing and setup at this stage prevent years of inefficiency and costly repairs down the road.

2. HVAC Maintenance Service

Routine HVAC maintenance service including filter changes, coil cleaning, and system inspections  extends equipment lifespan, keeps warranties valid, and catches small issues before they become expensive breakdowns.

3. Repairs and Troubleshooting

From strange noises to inconsistent temperatures, a qualified technician can diagnose and fix issues before they escalate.

4. Emergency Heating and Cooling Service

Furnace failures in winter or air conditioning breakdowns in summer rarely happen at a convenient time. A reliable emergency heating and cooling service ensures you’re never left without comfort or safety when it matters most.

Choosing the Right HVAC Contractor

Not all technicians are created equal. When selecting an HVAC contractor or air conditioning contractor, look for:

  • Licensed, insured, and certified technicians
  • Transparent, upfront pricing
  • Experience with both residential and commercial systems
  • Positive local reviews and references
  • Availability for emergency calls
  • Manufacturer-backed warranties on parts and labor

A trustworthy contractor doesn’t just fix the immediate problem, they help you understand your system and plan for long-term efficiency.

HVAC Services in Burnaby

If you’re searching for dependable HVAC Services Burnaby, local expertise matters. Weather patterns, building codes, and regional energy costs all influence what type of heating and cooling setup works best in this area. A local team understands these factors and can recommend solutions tailored to Burnaby homes and businesses, not generic, one-size-fits-all fixes.

At Airlinx Heating, our technicians specialize in everything from routine maintenance to full system installations, backed by local knowledge and responsive service.

Signs You Need Professional HVAC Help

Watch for these warning signs that it’s time to call a professional:

  • Uneven heating or cooling between rooms
  • Rising energy bills without increased usage
  • Strange noises, odors, or excessive dust
  • Frequent cycling on and off
  • Weak airflow from vents
  • System age of 10–15+ years

Catching these signs early  and scheduling regular HVAC maintenance service  can save you from a full system failure and costly emergency repairs.

Final Thoughts

So, what is HVAC? It’s the essential system that keeps your indoor environment safe, comfortable, and efficient  covering heating, ventilation, and air conditioning as one integrated network. Understanding how it works empowers you to make smarter decisions about installation, maintenance, and repairs.

Whether you need routine upkeep, a new system installation, or an emergency heating and cooling service, working with an experienced, licensed HVAC contractor ensures your investment pays off in comfort and reliability for years to come.

Ready to upgrade your comfort? Contact Airlinx Heating today for expert HVAC Services Burnaby, from installation to emergency repairs  and experience the difference a trusted local team makes.

title.rendered: How to Keep Mice Out of Heat Pump and Prevent Costly Damage

content.rendered:
Have you ever opened up your outdoor unit only to see some chewed wires, shredded insulation, and even a suspicious nest hidden between panels? Well, then you know first-hand just how frustrating the presence of mice in your heat pump can get. Rodents are naturally attracted by warmth, safety, and quiet environment offered by your heat pump, particularly once the weather starts getting colder. A neglected rodent infestation can easily escalate from a tune-up to a pricey heat pump repair job.

But what you should know is that preventing mice from nesting in your heat pump doesn’t take too much effort. Some regular maintenance and prevention tips can save your heat pump from unnecessary problems. Read on to find out more.

Why Do Mice Like Heat Pumps?

Heat pumps are the perfect home for mice because of how warm and comfortable they are and how many places there are to hide. Throw in some leaves or tall grass in the surrounding area, and the mouse will feel right at home.

Mice are specifically drawn to:

  • The heat emitted from the refrigerant lines and electrical components
  • Hard-to-reach spots within the outer housing
  • Materials used for nesting such as leaves, grass, and loose insulation
  • Any nearby food or water sources, even if they are just a couple of feet away

As soon as the mice start to take up residence, you know that they will not be sitting idly by. They can chew the wires, nest the motor fans, or plug up condensate lines and drains. Each of these can result in short circuits, reduced air flow, or shut down your entire system.

Signs That You May Have a Mouse Problem

Before going into how to prevent mouse problems, it is important to recognize the signs. These include:

  • Droppings or pieces of nesting material inside or around the unit
  • Damaged wires or frayed insulation
  • Scurrying, scratching, or rustling noises from within the cabinet
  • A system that doesn’t work properly or turns off without reason
  • A damp or mildew smell, or even the smell of burning around the electrical panel
  • Weaker heating

It might be time to get a professional in there if you see any of these signs.

Easy Tips for Stopping Mice From Getting into Your Heat Pump

Clear the Area Around the Unit

Rodents love messiness, so the simplest first step would be to tidy up. Leave several feet of unobstructed area around the heat pump. It should not be surrounded by any leaves, mulch, and any other lawn debris. Also, cut off any bushes and branches touching the cabinet of the heat pump. Do not pile firewood and storage boxes nearby. If water is prone to accumulate in the soil close to the heat pump, solve this problem too. Wet soil, like hot one, will attract more pests.

A pleasant additional trick: some plants, such as rosemary, mint, lavender, and garlic are proven to repel mice. So plant them some distance away from the heat pump (not right next to it).

Seal the Openings

This is probably the best measure you can take. Rodents can squeeze into openings smaller than a coin. You should look for openings around:

  • Refrigerant line penetrations where pipes go through the wall or the heat pump itself
  • Wiring holes and conduit openings
  • Bottom panels, base pads, and access covers
  • Fan grills and cabinet seams

The fact that the cracks are filled by steel wool is a great way of sealing the space because the mice won’t chew through this material. The other two good options include stainless steel mesh or hardware cloth with openings of 1/4 inch, whereas the best way of achieving a permanent solution will be combining the steel wool with the silicone caulk. However, it is better not to use expanding foam because the mice will chew through it.

Add Physical Barriers

Beyond sealing, a few physical upgrades go a long way:

  • Fine wire mesh over vents and openings, while still allowing proper airflow
  • Line-set covers with tight-fitting ends
  • Elevating the unit slightly, since narrow legs or stands are harder for mice to climb
  • A small protective enclosure with fine mesh, as long as it doesn’t block ventilation

A qualified technician can install these without affecting how your heat pump system performs.

Go for Natural Deterrents

In case you want to go chemical-free, here are some natural deterrence methods that you may try:

  • Cotton balls dipped in peppermint oil at the entry points
  • Cedar shavings or pine shavings at the base
  • Dryer sheets or strongly scented bars of soap to be changed once in a while

You can also use ultrasonic deterrents as an additional option. Just remember not to put any poison close to the system. A mouse that dies inside the cabinet can create an even bigger mess and odor problem than the original infestation.

Why Maintenance Is Needed

It is necessary to maintain the heat pump system on a regular basis because it will help us to identify the cause of the problem in the early stages. In addition to maintaining the system, the technician will be able to detect any signs of nesting, clear the debris from the system, inspect the wiring, and check if there is any damage to the seals or access panels. It would be twice a year for most homeowners.

A Quick Prevention Checklist

  • Clear leaves, mulch, and vegetation from around the unit
  • Seal gaps with steel wool, mesh, or silicone
  • Install rodent guards or fine mesh screens
  • Use natural repellents near entry points
  • Book professional maintenance twice a year
  • Keep trash, pet food, and bird feeders away from the unit

When to Hire a Professional

As soon as you detect signs of nesting, damaged wiring, or any other changes which are affecting the performance of the heat pump system, you should turn to professionals for help and not try to fix the issue yourself. Doing the work related to electrical parts can be dangerous without proper knowledge and training, so a Airlinx will be able to do all the work right the first time in Burnaby and nearby areas.

Conclusion

Though mice are relatively small animals, their impact on a heat pump system is quite damaging and can cost a lot of money. But the good news is that all you need to prevent them from entering the system is just some preventive measures.

title.rendered: Why You Should be Doing Regular Air Conditioning Service?

content.rendered:
Regular AC service is crucial to keep your air conditioning unit running more efficiently. It is a better investment in the long run, as it saves you a lot of money. AC service not only prevents damages but also keeps on increasing the lifespan of your AC unit. Yes, many people tend to ignore AC service and call for an AC service technician, only after its breakdown. But this can cause a huge dent in their pocket, as necessary repair can cost a lot.

An AC conditioning unit results in more wear and tear. Also, an AC working in poor condition can lead to consuming more energy to function in a normal way. So, if your AC service is performed regularly, then it will perform ideally. Hence, get your AC service done at least once a year.

 

Here are the reasons why you should do regular AC servicing

 

1. It improves air quality:

AC service performed regularly ensures clean air filters. Your AC unit carries air inside your home regularly, which passes through vents, ducts, and filters. Over some time dust, dirt and bacteria will gather within your AC unit and will make your indoor air quality very poor.

This can lead to some serious health issues like allergies, asthma, lung infection, etc. Air conditioning service regularly helps to improve air quality and will help in spreading clean air around your room.

 

 2. It increases life span:

If AC servicing is done regularly, then your AC unit needs no replacement. AC servicing is needed to make sure that your air conditioner is working fine and it also helps in increasing the lifespan of your unit in the long run. An AC service technician will fix small faults and will help in avoiding big damage in the future.

 

3. It reduces breakdown:

An AC technician will help in checking all your parts, and cleaning them and will make sure that your filters should be replaced timely. This helps in reducing a major breakdown. Airlinx is a one-stop solution for all your AC-related problems, repair requests, and complaints.

 

4. It helps in saving energy costs:

An air conditioner uses less energy if it is free from all leaks and clogs. A regular AC service will also decrease your electricity bill which will burn less energy and will save you money. It will also be responsible for efficient cooling and airflow.

 

5. It prevents expensive replacement:

A maintained air conditioner would not require replacement. Replacement of an AC is too costly. Therefore, it is mandatory to get your regular AC servicing, which will save costs and will provide better cooling. Your air conditioning unit will also last for a long.

 

6. It removes bad air:

An air conditioning unit sometimes releases a bad odor. This is because of bacteria, fungus, and dirt stored in your AC unit which is normal. So, in this case, you need an AC service technician to check the condition of your air conditioner and free your home from bad odor.

 

7. To remain cool:

Regular AC servicing helps in ensuring proper cooling. If the air conditioner breaks down then this will make your home environment uncomfortable and hot. Therefore, a yearly AC servicing will help you and will make sure that your AC runs smoothly and effectively.

 

Why is it necessary to do regular AC servicing?

 

Regular servicing of your air conditioner involves dirty components like condenser, air filter, and oiling the fan motors if needed. The professional who conducts the service will also make sure to fix any damaged or worn components that need replacement. They will also make sure that everything is working correctly like system pressures and temperatures, thermostats, safety devices, and sensors.

So, is it time to get your air conditioner serviced? If yes, then Airlinx can assist you. We have years of experience in servicing, and repairing your air conditioners. So, get in touch with us and we would help you reap all the benefits of a regular air conditioning service.

title.rendered: 5 Common Causes To Do Regular Heating And Air Conditioning Services

content.rendered:
The invention of the heating and air conditioning systems played a crucial role in making a man’s life easy. Yes, apart from making indoor temperatures bearable during winters and summers, heating and air conditioning systems are bliss to us. But it is extremely crucial to know when our homes need air conditioning and heating maintenance and repair services. Because if these things fail, our entire system will fail. Also, failure to observe such attentiveness results in unexpected and inconvenient breakdowns, which can result in increased costs.

Also, implementing timely heating and air conditioning repairs has several health benefits which include stopping the survival of harmful insects like mosquitoes and ants which reduces the growth of mold that cause allergic reactions. So, it is always necessary to look out for the following indicators of problems that are associated with heating and air conditioning units.

Unpleasant burning odors coming out from HVAC units:

Heating and cooling units have nothing to do with how your home smells like. But a burning or pungent smell coming from your unit, especially when switching it on, could be an indicator that your home needs professional heating and air conditioning repair services. In this condition, a burning smell denotes an underlying insulation issue whereby a wire, rubber, or piece of plastic could have burned out causing the odor.

And other times, if you encounter an unpleasant odor, it indicates the growth of mold within the air conditioning and heating system. The mold formation can result in allergic reactions which can be fatal. Hence, homeowners should seek the best heating and air conditioning repair services whenever they find an unpleasant odor coming out from their heating and cooling systems.  

Increase in energy utility bills:

Through the constant repair and maintenance of your heating and cooling unit, you can improve its efficiency and reduce spending on bills. If you are paying a higher electric bill with time along with other indicators of heating and AC troubles, it could be because of the failure to seek timely heating and air conditioning repairs. The spike in energy costs results in substantial leakages.

The air conditioning system is getting warm air:

If you realize that the temperature in your home is not as cool as you expected, then you need to check the thermostat, switch it to a cooling mood, and keep on adjusting the temperature to one which is lower than the existing room conditions to deal with this issue. When that does not work and the vents on your air conditioning system keep blowing out warm air, then it could mean that your home needs instant heating and air conditioning repairs. HVAC professionals can help you resolve this issue and check your condenser issues and duct leakage problems. The refrigerant and compressor are crucial elements in the cooling process. They can be a bit complex hence reiterating the need to seek expert heating and AC repair services when you do not get enough cool air in your home.

Short cycling and a compressor which would keep on running always:

Short cycling is used by HVAC experts to describe heating and AC systems that cannot complete a cooling cycle. This causes the system to overheat and stop, hence it cannot complete its cooling cycle. Talking about a continuously running compressor, it is because your system might take too long to reach the optimum temperature. So, this also indicates that your home needs professional heating and air conditioning maintenance. HVAC specialists will evaluate the unit to determine the underlying problems and would suggest workable solutions for it.

Leaks around the air conditioning and heating unit:

Moisture leaks and accumulation around your home’s heating and cooling unit signify a serious issue because the system is designed in such a way that it needs to be dry. Such leaks might result from a broken condensate drain whose content will be poisonous. These leaks occur in various forms where you will notice water leaking directly out of cooling and heating units, or there is the formation of ice on the copper refrigerator lines outside the condenser.

Poor functionality of the air conditioning system can be another reason:

When you see that your air conditioning system is taking much longer time to maintain its regular airflow, then there is some serious issue within the AC apparatus. You may find out that the air is cool but the airflow is not strong. This could be a result of air duct blockages which might place extra strain on the air conditioning unit thus making it to work harder to deal with the inconsistencies in functionality.

As mentioned before, heating and air conditioning repair not only helps in keeping your home comfortable, but also assists in shielding your loved ones from harmful elements like mildew and mold. title.rendered: The Complete Guide to HVAC Services for Commercial Buildings and What You Need to Know

content.rendered:
When your Air conditioning or heating system breaks down, it is crucial to know whom to call for its repair. We will cover everything you need to know, from how the system works and what kind of maintenance is required for the right functioning.

We will also discuss common issues and how to troubleshoot them. So, whether you are a homeowner who needs to get that repair done, or you are someone looking for a qualified contractor, then you should read this article.

What is HVAC and how does it work?

Ventilation, heating, and air conditioning (HVAC) is a system that is used to regulate the humidity and temperature of your indoor spaces. It is an innovative technology that has changed over the years. With Airlinx heating and air-conditioning services, you get the best HVAC services.

The three main components of an HVAC system are the evaporator, condenser, and compressor. The work of a compressor is to pump coolant through the system. Then comes the evaporator, which removes heat from the air.

HVAC systems are used in both commercial and residential locations. These can be either decentralized or centralized. Centralized systems are more common in huge buildings, whereas decentralized units are common in smaller homes.

Most common types of HVAC systems:

Standard split systems:

A standard split system has an outdoor unit that envelopes the condenser and the compressor. This type of system is a good option for smaller homes because it is less expensive. Also, they are easier to maintain since the condenser and compressor units are present outside.

Do you know Packaged units?

A packaged unit is a self-contained HVAC system that has all the components in a single unit. The compressor, condenser, and evaporator are all clubbed together in the same outdoor unit. This is a good choice for larger homes because it is more efficient. Also, packaged units are much easier to install since everything is in the same place.

Heard about ductless mini-split systems?

It is similar to a standard split system, which does not use ductwork. It has one or more indoor units which are connected to an outdoor unit with the help of refrigerant lines. This is a good choice for homes or businesses that do not have existing ductwork.

Geothermal heat pumps are great:

A geothermal heat pump uses water to heat and cool your home. The water has a constant temperature that is lower than the air during hot days and cold in the winter.

This type of system is a good option for businesses and homes that can be very efficient. Also, geothermal heat pumps last more.

Necessary HVAC maintenance tips:

So, once you have your HVAC systems installed, it is necessary to keep up with regular maintenance. It helps in ensuring that your system is running efficiently and can prevent costly repairs. So, here are a few maintenance tips that will benefit you:

Changing your air filters regularly:

This is one of the most easiest and important things you can do to maintain your HVAC systems. Your filters need to be changed regularly every month or two. But this depends on the type of filter you have and the environment in which you live.

Cleaning your coils:

The condenser coils and the evaporator might get dirty over time. So, this reduces the efficiency of the system and causes it to work harder than it needs. Cleaning your coils at least once a year is the need of an hour.

Checking your ductwork:

Ductwork might leak over time. This results in higher energy bills and reduced indoor air quality. So, it is a good idea to get your ductwork checked every few years to make sure it is working properly.

HVAC repair tips:

 It might happen that even with regular maintenance, your HVAC systems can break down from time to time. So, here are a few tips for troubleshooting common HVAC problems:

Checking the thermostat:

If your system isn’t working, make sure you check the thermostat. There is a possibility that it might not be set correctly. So, get this fixed.

Checking the pilot light:

Your unit’s pilot is a crucial component. So, if it is out, the unit won’t function properly. Simply relight the pilot light and check to see if the unit starts functioning again.

Checking the circuit breaker:

If your system stops working suddenly, then the circuit breaker may have been tripped. This is common in houses that have older electrical systems.

title.rendered: Why You Need a Heating and Air Conditioning Repair in Your Home

content.rendered:
You can find Air conditioners in almost 90% of homes across Canada. Sometimes, it is too hot in British Columbia. Also, we love enjoying our cool and comfortable spaces away from the scorching heat.

But, there is nothing worse than an air conditioner’s breakdown. So, having an AC repair service technician helping you to do your regular maintenance at the beginning of the season can save you from that uncomfortable situation.

So, here are ten reasons why taking advantage of this kind of service will make a huge difference in your life.

1. Extending your air conditioner’s life:

There are so many reasons why an AC unity may not be functioning properly. In the majority of cases, many minor problems need easy fixes. But if they are not taken care of promptly, then that will create some more issues which can ruin your system altogether. So, the solution to this problem is doing regular maintenance check-ups.

When a technician inspects the system, they identify the minor issues and then resolve them.

HVAC systems are not cheap to install, so you need to take extra care to protect that investment.

2. Purifying air quality:

An air conditioner does more than just pump cold air into your home. Many systems contribute to purifying your very crucial air quality.

As the air moves through the system, it passes through a filtration system. Thus, depending on the exact filters, the contaminants found in the system will be cleaned out.

Also, when the system does not receive regular cleanings, those filters begin to fill up. The more they filter out, the more junk stays inside them. And this might then result in the malfunctioning of the system. Also, a dirty air filter can do the opposite of its intended purpose by putting contaminants in the air. An AC repair service will make sure that the system’s filters are cleaned and allow good air to enter the house.

3. It reduces humidity indoors:

The benefits of AC repair include reducing humidity inside your home. While the air is moving through the filtration and cooling system, the excess water is also being drawn out of it.

Humidity inside your home is a problem because it can lead to issues like mold or mildew. This results in some serious health issues, especially respiratory problems. A high-humidity house will also have a musty smell throughout, which is not pleasant.

So, the main goal of an air conditioning system is to make your home more comfortable. High humidity is not comfortable at all. Heat in humidity feels much hotter.

An HVAC service expert checks the system’s humidity levels within your home and helps you make decisions based on the results.

4.  Increasing the system’s efficiency:

 An ineffective air conditioning system does more than just make your home hot. It can result in costing you a ton of money throughout the summer season. So, repairing your AC as the weather begins to warm up can help in saving you some money on your electricity bill every month. Beyond changing out filters, technicians can also check the other aspects of the machine. It includes fins and coils.

Both these parts can get worn out over time. And if this happens, then the whole unit would not be able to function correctly. An HVAC expert may be able to repair the damage done. They will have the training and knowledge to know which the more appropriate response is. The HVAC expert checks the condensation drain for build-up. This can result in major problems but can get fixed in most cases.

5. Improving health:

Contaminants and pollution in the air have a major effect on the wellness and health of those who are living with that air.

A system cleanout and repair session of an AC can have a great effect on those living in the home. This is true for people having respiratory issues.

A cooler house results in better sleep, which is vital to your overall health. People have an easier time falling asleep in a cooler environment. The ability to fall asleep can add precious resting time to a busy schedule that may not get otherwise. This cooler temperature allows people to stay asleep and delivers sound sleep because they are not comfortable with the heat.

6. Clearing out the unwanted pests:

During the summer months, we use our homes as a safe place away from all insects and bugs. So, when your air conditioner is not working then you will have to open the windows to get some fresh air. And even with the use of screens, bugs can still get in.

But if your unit is working and cooling your space off sufficiently then you would not need to have an access point for them. The filters that are a part of an air conditioning system do a great job of stopping any bugs from getting into the circulating air as well. This can be crucial for people who have allergies.

So, when your AC service expert is checking the filters, they also make sure to check the unit for new inhabitants.

7. Eliminating extra noise:

One of the biggest benefits of having HVAC routine maintenance is the elimination of noise.

All of us have experienced this, if you are having a conversation with your family member, AC kicks on. And all of a sudden you cannot hear them anymore. It is so annoying.

An AC unit that has not been serviced can get out of syn. The fan can shift things around and can cause different parts to be loosened.

An unserviced machine might also have to work harder to spin for better build-up. That build-up can be caused by condensation or debris. Trained AC experts have done so many repairs throughout their careers so that they can easily spot the noise.

 Most people rely heavily on air conditioners during the hot summer months. So, to make them work efficiently, simply call us and set up an appointment soon!
